nodes.name: Section 4.3, Section 4.4, Proposition 4.12, Theorem 4.17: *+[F] §§ -- Analytic continuation of the…
nodes.statement:
Define a linear transformation $\mathbb U^{\rm tw}_l 
\colon H_{{\operatorname{ext}}} \to H_{\operatorname{\text{CR}}}(\mathbb P(\underline{w}))$  
depending on $l\in \mathbb Z$ and the parameter $\xi = \lambda/z$ by 
\begin{equation} 
 
\mathbb U^{\rm tw}_l (\phi_{k-1}) = 
\frac{1}{d}  
\sum_{f\in \mathfrak{F}} \boldsymbol{1}_f 
\frac{\left(
\zeta^k e^{p+ 2\pi\mathtt{i}(\overline{f} + \frac{\xi}{d})}
\right)^l}
{\zeta^k e^{p+ 2\pi\mathtt{i} (\overline{f} +\frac{\xi}{d})}-1}
\prod_{j:kq_j\in \mathbb Z} (-q_j \xi), 
\quad k=1,\dots,d. 
\end{equation} 
Then we have 
\[
u^{-\xi} ({\mathfrak{H}}^{\rm tw}_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}})_{\rm continued} = 
\mathbb U^{\rm tw}_l \left({\mathfrak{H}}^{\rm tw}_{{\operatorname{FJRW}}}\right).    
\]
where $({\mathfrak{H}}^{\rm tw}_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}})_{\rm continued}$ is the analytic 
continuation of ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\rm tw}_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}}$ along the path $\gamma_l$.

Let $\mathbb U_l\colon H_{\operatorname{nar}}(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d) \to H_{\operatorname{amb}}(X_W)$ denote the 
map in Corollary 4.15. 
For a graded matrix factorization $E\in \operatorname{{MF}}^{\rm gr}_{\boldsymbol{\mu}_d}(W)$ 
such that ${\rm ch}(E) \in H_{\operatorname{nar}}(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d)$, we have 
\[
\mathbb U_l \left( \operatorname{inv}^* {\rm ch}(E)\right)  
= \operatorname{inv}^* {\rm ch} \left( \Phi_l (E) \right).  
\]

nodes.statement:
In both FJRW and GW theories, there exist 
$\overline{H}$-valued complex analytic functions 
$\Upsilon^{{\rm tw},\nu}$, $\nu\in B$ defined 
on an open set $\widehat{U} \times \mathbb C_z\times \mathbb C_\lambda
\subset \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \times \mathbb C_z \times \mathbb C_\lambda$ 
such that 
\begin{equation} 

L^{\rm tw}(\varsigma(x;\lambda),z;\lambda) I^{{\rm tw},\nu}(x, z;\lambda) 
= z \Upsilon^{{\rm tw},\nu}(x,z;\lambda).
\end{equation} 
Here $\varsigma$ denotes the mirror map (75) 
in each theory. 
The fundamental solution $L(\varsigma(x;\lambda),z;\lambda)$ is also 
analytic over $\widehat{U}\times \mathbb C_z^\times \times \mathbb C_\lambda$. 
The open subset $\widehat{U}\subset \widehat{\mathcal{M}}$ is of the form $\{|u|<\epsilon\}$ 
for FJRW theory and is of the form $\{|v|<\epsilon\}$ for GW theory.  
For $\nu=0$, we have $\Upsilon^{{\rm tw},0} = F\cdot T_0$ 
where $F$ is the function appearing in (74).

Via the $\widehat{\mathcal{R}}^{\rm tw}$-module $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}^{\rm tw}$ over $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}$, 
the $e_{\mathbb C^\times}$-twisted quantum connections $\nabla^{\rm tw}$ 
of FJRW theory and of GW theory 
are analytically continued to each other. 
More precisely, we have a local trivialization of $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}^{\rm tw}$ 
over $\widehat{U}_\heartsuit$ 
\begin{align*} 
\operatorname{Mir}_\heartsuit \colon 
\widehat{\mathcal{F}}^{\rm tw}|_{\widehat{U}_{\heartsuit} \times \mathbb C_z\times \mathbb C_\lambda} 
& \cong \overline{H}_\heartsuit 
\otimes \mathcal{O}_{\widehat{U}_{\heartsuit} \times \mathbb C_z\times \mathbb C_\lambda}, 
\quad 
\heartsuit = {\operatorname{FJRW}} \text{ or } \operatorname{\text{GW}} \\ 
\triangle_\nu & \longmapsto \Upsilon^{{\rm tw},\nu}_\heartsuit  
\end{align*}  
such that, under the trivialization, 
the action of $\widehat{\mathcal{R}}^{{\rm tw}}$ is 
given by the $e_{\mathbb C^\times}$-twisted quantum connection 
\[
z D \longmapsto \varsigma_\heartsuit^* \nabla^{{\rm tw},\heartsuit}_{zD}, \quad 
\text{$D$ is a vector field on $\widehat{U}_{\heartsuit}$,}
\]
where $\varsigma_\heartsuit \colon \widehat{U}_\heartsuit\times \mathbb C_\lambda
\to \overline{H}^{\le 2}_\heartsuit$ 
is the mirror map (75) in the respective theory.

nodes.name: Section 5.4, Theorem 2.23: *+[F] § Construction of the global $D$ -module $\mathcal{F}$ Proof of
nodes.statement:
There exists a locally free sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ over $\mathcal{M} \times \mathbb C_z$ 
with a meromorphic flat connection $\nabla$ (with simple poles 
along $z=0$) 
\[
\nabla \colon \mathcal{F} \to 
\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{M}\times \{0\}) \otimes \Omega_{\mathcal{M}\times \mathbb C_z}^1, 
\]
a $\nabla$-flat, symmetric and non-degenerate pairing 
\[
P \colon (-)^*\mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{F} \to z^{\hat{c}} \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}\times \mathbb C_z} 
\]
and a $\mathbb Z$-local subsystem $F_{\mathbb Z}$ of the same rank 
over $\mathcal{M}\times \mathbb C_z^\times$ 
\[
F_{\mathbb Z} \subset (\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{M} \times \mathbb C_z^\times})^\nabla 
\]
such that the following holds: 

{\rm (i)} For a small open neighbourhood 
$U_{{\operatorname{FJRW}}} = \{|u|<\epsilon\}\subset \mathcal{M}$ of the LG point, 
we have a mirror map $\tau_{\operatorname{_{FJRW}}} \colon U_{{\operatorname{FJRW}}} \to 
H^2_{\operatorname{nar}}(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d)/\langle G\rangle$ 
such that $\tau_{\operatorname{_{FJRW}}} = -u \phi_1 + O(u^2)$ and 
\[
(\mathcal{F}, \nabla, (-1)^{N-1}P, F_{\mathbb Z}) \Bigr |_{U_{\operatorname{FJRW}} \times \mathbb C_z} 
\cong \tau_{\operatorname{_{FJRW}}}^* 
\left( QDM_{\operatorname{nar}}(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d) /\langle G\rangle \right),   
\]
where in the right-hand side appears 
the narrow part quantum $D$-module (Definition 2.10) 
of $(\mathbb C^N, W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d)$ equipped with the $\widehat{\Gamma}$-integral 
structure (Definition 2.19) 
and $G$ is the Galois action (\S 2.4.3). 

{\rm (ii)} For a small open neighbourhood 
$U_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}} = \{|v|<\epsilon\}\subset \mathcal{M}$ 
of the large radius limit point, 
we have a mirror map 
$\tau_{\operatorname{_{GW}}} \colon U_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}} \to H^2_{\operatorname{amb}}(X_W)/\langle G\rangle$
such that $\tau_{\operatorname{_{GW}}}(v) = p \log v + O(v)$ and 
\[
(\mathcal{F}, \nabla, P, F_{\mathbb Z}) \Bigr |_{U_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}} \times \mathbb C_z} 
\cong \tau_{\operatorname{_{GW}}}^*\left( 
QDM_{\operatorname{amb}}(X_W)/\langle G\rangle \right),   
\] 
where in the right-hand side appears 
the ambient part quantum $D$-module of $X_W$ 
equipped with the $\widehat{\Gamma}$-integral structure
and $G$ is the Galois action.

nodes.name: Section 5.5, Theorem 2.25: *+[F] § Reconstruction of big quantum $D$ -modules Proof of
nodes.statement:
Assume that $X_W$ is a manifold. 

{\rm (i)} The ``big" quantum product of $(\mathbb C^N,W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d)$ 
on the narrow part 
and the ``big" quantum product of $X_W$ 
on the ambient part 
are convergent in the sense of \S 2.4.1. 

{\rm (ii)} 
The global $D$-module $(\mathcal{F},\nabla,P,F_{\mathbb Z})$ 
in Theorem 2.23 can be extended to 
a $D$-module $(\mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}},\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}},P^{\operatorname{ext}},F_{\mathbb Z}^{\operatorname{ext}})$ 
over a base $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}\times \mathbb C_z$, 
where $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}$ is a complex manifold 
of dimension $\operatorname{rank} \mathcal{F} = \dim H_{\operatorname{amb}}(X_W)$ which contains 
a Zariski open subset $\mathcal{M}'$ of $\mathcal{M}$ as a 
submanifold. 
The extended $D$-module is identified 
with the ``big" narrow/ambient part quantum $D$-module 
of FJRW/GW theory in a 
neighbourhood of $U_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}}$ or $U_{{\operatorname{FJRW}}}$.  

More precisely, there exists a locally free sheaf 
$\mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}}$ over $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}\times \mathbb C_z $
equipped with a meromorphic flat connection $\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}}$ 
(with poles of order two along $z=0$)
\[
\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}} \colon \mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}} \to \mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}}(\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}
\times \{0\}) \otimes \left (
\pi^* \Omega_{\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}}^1 
\oplus \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}} \times \mathbb C_z} \frac{\mathsf{d} z}{z} 
\right), 
\]
where $\pi \colon \mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}} \times \mathbb C_z \to \mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}$ 
is the projection, 
a $\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}}$-flat, symmetric and non-degenerate 
pairing 
\[
P^{\operatorname{ext}} \colon (-)^* \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{F} \to z^{\hat{c}} \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}} \times \mathbb C_z} 
\]
and a $\mathbb Z$-local subsystem $F^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\mathbb Z}$ of the same rank 
over $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}} \times \mathbb C^\times_z$ 
\[
F^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\mathbb Z} \subset (\mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}}|_{\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}\times \mathbb C^\times_z})^{\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}}} 
\]
such that the following holds: 
























\begin{itemize} 
\item $(\mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}},\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}}, P^{\operatorname{ext}}, F_{\mathbb Z}^{\operatorname{ext}})|_{\mathcal{M}'} 
= (\mathcal{F},\nabla,P,F_{\mathbb Z})|_{\mathcal{M}'}$; 





\item 
There exist open neighbourhoods  
$U_\heartsuit^{\operatorname{ext}}$ of $U_{\heartsuit}$ in $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ext}}$ 
and open embeddings 
\[
\tau^{{\operatorname{ext}}}_\heartsuit \colon 
U_\heartsuit^{\operatorname{ext}} \hookrightarrow H'_\heartsuit/\langle G\rangle, 
\quad \tau^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\heartsuit}|_{U_{\heartsuit}} = \tau_{\heartsuit}
\]
for $\heartsuit = \operatorname{\text{GW}}$ and ${\operatorname{FJRW}}$ 
such that we have isomorphisms  
\begin{align*} 
(\mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}},\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}},(-1)^{N-1} P^{\operatorname{ext}}, F_{\mathbb Z}^{\operatorname{ext}}) 
|_{U^{\operatorname{ext}}_{{\operatorname{FJRW}}}}  
& \cong {\tau^{{\operatorname{ext}}}_{\operatorname{_{FJRW}}}}^*
(QDM_{\operatorname{nar}}(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d)/\langle G\rangle) \\ 
(\mathcal{F}^{\operatorname{ext}},\nabla^{\operatorname{ext}},P^{\operatorname{ext}}, F_{\mathbb Z}^{\operatorname{ext}}) |_{U^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{\text{GW}}}}  
& \cong {\tau^{{\operatorname{ext}}}_{\operatorname{_{GW}}}}^*  
(QDM_{\operatorname{amb}}(X_W) /\langle G \rangle). 
\end{align*} 
\end{itemize}

nodes.name: Section 5.6, Theorem 2.26: *+[F] § Global monodromy autoequivalences Proof of
nodes.statement:
The $\mathbb Z$-local system $F_{\mathbb Z}$ of the global $D$-module 
$(\mathcal{F},\nabla,P,F_{\mathbb Z})$ in Theorem 2.23 
induces the representation of the quiver of Figure fig:paths_in_M 
given by the assignment $b_0 \mapsto N'(X_W)$, 
$b_\infty\mapsto N'(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d)$ and   
\begin{alignat*}{2} 


\gamma_{\operatorname{CY}} &  \longmapsto  \ &  \mathcal{O}(-1) & 
\colon  N'(X_W) \to N'(X_W) \\ 
\gamma_{\operatorname{LG}} &  \longmapsto  \ &(1) & 
\colon  N'(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d) \to N'(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d) \\ 
\gamma_l^{-1} &  \longmapsto  \ & \Phi_l & 
\colon  N'(W,\boldsymbol{\mu}_d) \to N'(X_W) \\ 
\gamma_{\operatorname{con}}^{-1} & \longmapsto \ & T_{\mathcal{O}} & 
\colon N'(X_W) \to N'(X_W) 

\end{alignat*} 
where $\mathcal{O}(-1)$ denotes the tensor product by $\mathcal{O}(-1)$, 
$(1)$ denotes the shift of the grading by $1$,  
$\Phi_l$ denotes the Orlov equivalence (\S 4.2) 
defined for $l\in \mathbb Z$ and 
$T_{\mathcal{O}}$ denotes the Seidel-Thomas spherical twist 
(\S 5.6) by the structure sheaf. 
Moreover, the monodromy representation 
\[
\rho \colon \pi_1(\mathcal{M}, b_0) \to \operatorname{Aut}(N'(X_W),\chi)
\]
can be lifted to a group homomorphism 
\[
\hat{\rho} \colon \pi_1(\mathcal{M},b_0)
\to \operatorname{Auteq}(D^b(X_W))/[2], 
\] 
where $[2]$ is the $2$-shift functor.
